A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Length Generalization Bounds for Transformers by the same authors. Their main text, equations, Figure 1, references, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite reorganization.

before.justification: v1 presents mathematical constructions, bounds, and proofs. Its empirical examples are attributed to prior publications; neither the main text nor appendices report original empirical results.

after.justification: v2 remains a theoretical paper. The expanded discussion and appendix comparison summarize prior work without adding original experiments, simulations, or data analyses.

M1.justification: The C-RASP/C-RASP+ constructions and transformer computations are retained. Explicitly naming the two regimes as (1, log n)-precision and (1, 1)-precision replaces terminology already defined in v1, without changing the models or procedures.

E1.justification: Neither version conducts dataset-based training or evaluation. MAJORITY and bounded-depth Dyck languages remain theoretical examples, not added evaluation tasks.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods experimentally. The expanded comparison with Izzo et al. concerns theoretical assumptions, not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Neither version reports an original experimental protocol. The settings listed in new Appendix A.2 describe prior theoretical models, not experiments conducted by this work.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests, or empirical supplementary analyses are added or removed. The Dyck-language argument and its geometric illustration are retained; the new Lipschitz discussion is conceptual.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repetitions, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Section 6 revises cited length-generalization examples from N-to-3N and N-to-10N to 50-to-150 and 40-to-500, adding attribution to Deletang et al. These are changed literature examples, not original experiments or demonstrated same-setting performance gains. The paper's own bounds remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The substantive definitions, undecidability reduction, exponential bounds, simulation proofs, and depth-two reduction are retained. Lemma 4.5's proof moves from v1 Appendix A into Section 4, and the Dyck definition added to Example 2.3 already appeared in v1 Appendix B. The new prior-work discussion supplies no new proof or formal separation.

C1.justification: The central uncomputable-versus-exponential bound claims remain. v2 qualifies informal Theorem 1.1 with termination and Theorem 1.2 with worst-case necessity, and Section 6 explicitly positions the contribution as the first length-complexity bounds for entire transformer classes.

C2.justification: v2 adds a rationale connecting the idealized learner with complete bounded-length data and perfect optimization to practical learning difficulties. It identifies non-Lipschitz operations as a possible explanation for differences from Izzo et al., and distinguishes maximum training length from sample count, leaving potentially polynomial sample complexity open.

D1.justification: The precision representations, rounding rules, and simulation constructions in v1 Appendix C are retained in v2 Appendix B. No implementation instructions, hardware specifications, hyperparameters, or code/data access information are added.

R1.justification: The brief reference to Izzo et al. becomes a substantial comparison in Section 3.3 and new Appendix A.2, detailing both model variants and explaining possible compatibility with this paper's bounds. v2 also revises its positioning against Salzer et al., explicitly claiming a stronger undecidability result for a more restricted class. Deletang et al. is added, while several empirical-method and auxiliary references are removed; the Izzo publication update itself is not a new cited work.

P1.justification: v2 edits and condenses introductory material, expands the discussion, standardizes precision terminology, and updates publication and acknowledgement text. Lemma 4.5's proof moves into the main text, and the appendices are reorganized, while the main section sequence and most technical prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Lemma 4.2's inline bullet formulas become aligned display equations, and the relocated Lemma 4.5 proof changes from appendix to main-text formatting. Publication information and text placement change locally. Figure 1 and its caption are unchanged, and neither version contains experimental result tables.

improvement.justification: v2 improves clarity through explicit precision labels, termination and worst-case qualifications, and a detailed account of the assumptions behind potentially conflicting prior bounds. Moving Lemma 4.5's proof into Section 4 also improves accessibility. These are useful refinements to unchanged theoretical results; the Lipschitz explanation remains tentative rather than establishing a new separation.
